$x^(―) = 2.36, x^{2}^(―) = 18.62$

We wish to carry out a hypothesis test at a $5%$ significance level to determine whether there is sufficient evidence that the population variance $σ^{2}$ is greater than $10$.

The table below shows the values $χ_{ν, p}$ such that $P(X > χ_{ν, p}) = p$ for some particular values of $ν$ and $p$, where $X$ follows a chi-square distribution $χ^{2}(ν)$ with $ν$ degrees of freedom.

| $ν∖p$ | $0.995$ | $0.975$ | $0.950$ | $0.050$ | $0.025$ | $0.005$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| $64$ | $38.610$ | $43.776$ | $46.595$ | $83.675$ | $88.004$ | $96.878$ |
| $65$ | $39.383$ | $44.603$ | $47.450$ | $84.821$ | $89.177$ | $98.105$ |
| $66$ | $40.158$ | $45.431$ | $48.305$ | $85.965$ | $90.349$ | $99.330$ |

Using this information, select the options that make the following statements true.

The test statistic for this test is approximately
